President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Right. To your question, Rachel, you know, that dynamic in the pharma really speaks to, you know, pressure on the LC business.
Rachel Vatnsdal
Executive Director, JP Morgan
Okay. And then I just wanted to ask about monthly trends. You know, some of your peers have talked about how spending has been a little bit slow out of the gate in January and then into early February. So I guess since you guys have a few more weeks of visibility here, can you walk us through, were you seeing similar trends on just slower, slower spending to start the year? And has any of that started to come back? Any color there as we enter fiscal Q2 will be helpful. Thanks.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Well, as you know, I've been in this business for a while, and it's always slow in January. And that's why we have the seasonality we talked about relative to Q2. So I don't think we're seeing any significantly different trends than we've seen historically. Padraig, I know that you're closer than I am, but,
Phil Binns
President of the Agilent Life Science and Applied Markets Group, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, no, I think, I think that's right. That's right, Mike. I think on the ACG side, we see a number of service con- our service contract-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah
Phil Binns
President of the Agilent Life Science and Applied Markets Group, Agilent Technologies
Business comes in strong under the ACG side, but on the capital side, we're not seeing much.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, to put a finer point on that, January came in as we expected.
Operator
Our next question will come from the line of Vijay Kumar with Evercore ISI. Please go ahead.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
Hey, this is Jordan on for Vijay.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Okay.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
Hey, Mike, it's this is Jordan. Thanks for taking-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Hi, Jordan.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
-my question.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Sure.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
Maybe, maybe one follow-up on the China side. Have you seen any hints of stimulus to start the year? And if we do see a stimulus, do you have any foresight to what implications that will have on Agilent?
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
I have to have both Padraig and I in the conference room shaking our head, "No," we've not heard anything about any potential stimulus. And what I can tell you is, if it does happen, it's upside to our, our outlook.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
Understood. And then, maybe one more from me. Can you talk about how pricing has trended in the quarter and any updates to your expectations for the remainder of the year?
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Bob, do you want to, you want to take that one?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, we were pleased with the results. It was between 1% and 2%, so, but in line with kind of the seasonality and the mix that we saw, we would expect to see in Q1. So, you know, right now, it's on track. As we've talked about, you know, our consumables business and ACG business have the greatest price realization, followed by, generally speaking, actually, we had a very good result in diagnostics and genomics in the quarter, and then we did see some mix, but not anything out of the ordinary in the instrumentation side.
So all in, we're on track for what we expected for the full year.
[Company Representative] (Evercore ISI)
Company Representative, Evercore ISI
Understood. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Patrick Donnelly with Citi. Please go ahead.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
Hey, guys, thanks for taking the questions.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Sure.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
Yeah, Mike, I'll second the congratulations on the retirement. Bob, maybe one for you first. Just in terms of the EPS guide, it looks like you guys got an additional $20 million on the kind of net interest, other income. Can you just kind of flag, you know, if that's rolling through, you know, did that core earnings number move a little lower? Is there any moving pieces there? Then secondarily, just on the margin piece, you guys have that cost savings plan. Can you just talk about how that paces as the year goes? Would be helpful.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah. Thanks, Patrick. Great question, and what I would say is a couple of things. Yeah, we are on track to have more interest income than what we anticipated at the beginning of the year, that $20 million, and saw some of that in Q1 as well, and that's really a result of actually having better than expected cash flow in Q1 and great work by that treasury team. I would say that on, you know, the savings, we're on track for the savings targets for the full year.
And, you know, as I think about the year, it's still very early in the year, and this provides us what I would say is more confidence in the guide.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
... Okay, that's helpful. And then maybe just on kind of the book-to-bill, how are you guys thinking about, I think it's last quarter, you said, you know, the book-to-bill for the year would be above one, but you'd have quarters kind of in and out on the instrument side, which obviously we're seeing this quarter. How are you thinking about just the order trends and the book-to-bill trends on the instrument side as we work our way through the year, given what you're seeing today?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, no change to what we said back in November. You know, Q1 is a proof point for what we said.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
All right, fair enough. Thank you, guys.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
All right.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Dan Brennan with TD Cowen. Please go ahead.
Dan Brennan
Analyst, TD Cowen
Thank you. Mike, it's been great working with you over the last nine years, so congrats, and Padraig, look forward to working with you as well.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Thanks, Dan.
Dan Brennan
Analyst, TD Cowen
Maybe just, don't want to beat a dead horse, but just for the instruments, did you guys say... I know in the queue, you usually put out what the instrument number actually was. So what did actually instruments do in the quarter? And then, given how much easier comps go as we get through the year, can you just kind of give us a sense of pacing, like what, what should we expect on Q2 on instruments, and then we can, you know, kind of have at the back half of the year?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Well, I know the team did a calculation on that because the LSAG was down eleven, but that includes our consumables business, which was up. Yeah, I would say that, you know, we typically don't give all that information, but it was down. You know, we were down 11%. It was down twenty percent in the quarter. But that was better than expected, offset by, you know, 6% growth in our consumables business. If we look at the LSAG thinking for Q2, it's down low teens.
And a lot of that has to do with some of the timing associated with that $15 million shift. That's almost all capital equipment from Q2 back into Q1.
So if you look at it, it is in line with where we expect it to be. And then we go into more favorable compares in Q3 and Q4.
Dan Brennan
Analyst, TD Cowen
Correct. Correct. Got it. Okay. And then I know there's been a handful of questions already on China, but can you just, would you mind spending a bit more color on kind of what, maybe by segment, pharma, applied, any color you can give us, kind of what you're seeing within the different businesses in China, and is down mid-single still the expectation for China for the full year, or is there a chance you can kind of see some upside to that number? Thank you.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
I think we-- Bob, I think we've, we have, raised it up a bit.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
It's still down, but-- Yeah, yeah. I think, you know, we're cautiously optimistic there. I'd say it's still within a range that we had before, so I don't want to call an inflection. But if you looked at the markets, you know, we were down, you know, that 9% was roughly down 20-ish% in pharma. So, you know, that continues to be the area of really around the globe, but China's no different.
The great thing is, many of the other markets perform much better. So even when you think about, like, academia and government, that grew, so did our chem and advanced material business. Now, it grew very low single digits.
And then our forensics and environmental was down low single digits. So you're actually starting to see you know this stable you know continued stabilization, and then you'll get into you know very much easier compares in the back half of the year in China, 'cause you know that down 22% was down you know compared to up 12% last year. We had another strong compare in Q2, and then we actually started seeing the pretty significant declines year on year.
And so there's reasons to be optimistic about that continued stabilization that Mike talked about. But we're not ready yet to call an inflection you know, but when it happens, we'll take it. And Padraig, I think you wanted to jump in on this as well.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
Yeah, and I think, you know, what we see is also consumables and services continue to outperform expectations in China. So that's going to-
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah.
Patrick Donnelly
Managing Director, Citi
We expect that to continue.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
I think the story that -- great build, Padraig. I think the story really was in pharma, you know, Q1, you know, the instrument, the CapEx side of things. But we're pleased with the start there.
Dan Brennan
Analyst, TD Cowen
Great. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Catherine Schulte with Baird. Please go ahead.
Catherine Schulte
Analyst, Baird
Hey, guys. Thanks for the questions. Maybe first, then, pharma was down 12% in the quarter. I think you said biopharma was up 2% ex-China. What was small molecule performance ex-China, and maybe the outlook for biopharma versus small molecule for the rest of the year?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
So small molecule on a global basis was down, you know, roughly 18%, and it was ex-China, it was down 20%, and down, you know, roughly 14% for China. So pretty consistent across the globe. I would say in China, the big area in China that has been impacted is on the small molecule side, where we'll start to see better comps going forward after Q2.
Catherine Schulte
Analyst, Baird
Okay, and then maybe on consumables, great to see a return to growth there this quarter. Can you talk through what you saw outside of China on the consumable side?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Our consumables business was pretty consistent across the globe in terms of growth. So I don't know if you have anything you want to add to that on the what we've seen in consumables. I think we're really pleased to see that because it really speaks to the lab activity being robust. So, anything else you want to jump in on with?
Phil Binns
President of the Agilent Life Science and Applied Markets Group, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, probably just one item there, Mike. I think, we are seeing really good traction around our workflow development, so end-to-end solutions, which obviously is also drives our services business, as well, but, but around the consumables.
... the, in most of our end markets, we've been pretty heavily focused on developing workflows and making our customers' lives easier, and more integrated in their labs, and that's showing some really good, really good traction, and that's reflected in, solid, you know, connect and attach rates, in the, in the consumable space.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, thanks, Phil. I'm really glad you closed with the comments about connect rates. We talked about that relative to our services business. We're also seeing a very strong positive trend on consumables as well, which bodes well to our, our future in terms of recurrent revenue business growth.
Catherine Schulte
Analyst, Baird
All right, great. Thanks, and congrats on the retirement, Mike.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Thank you very much. Most appreciated.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Jack Meehan with Nephron Research. Please go ahead.
Jack Meehan
Analyst, Nephron Research
Thank you. Good afternoon, and Mike, again, it's been a pleasure working with you. Just had a couple of follow-ups. The first one was, can you just talk about what you're seeing in the genomics business within DG? I know it's still been a bit of a drag. Just when do you think that's going to start to turn?
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, thanks for your kind comments, Jack, and I think I'll invite Bob in on this one. But I think it's been sort of a tale of two cities. When we talk about our genomics business, there's really two pieces to it. Half of it's in QA/QC activities for NGS workflows, and we're seeing, you know, really solid growth in the consumables on that side of things, as well as you're starting to see signs of life on the CapEx, not ready to call the turn there yet, but that's in a reasonably good shape.
I think we've seen really in our US-based genomics business, you know, some real market challenges have been hitting us. And Bob, maybe you can elaborate on that.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, that's right. Thanks, Mike. As you said, you know, our NGS QC portfolio from an instrument and consumable side actually grew mid single digits in the quarter, which was very nice. The genomics chemistry side that we referenced in the prepared remarks was down. We faced some very difficult comps. We had a couple of companies that reorganized and exited some businesses. They had some lifetime buys at the end of Q1. I would expect that the performance of that to improve starting in the second half of the year.
Jack Meehan
Analyst, Nephron Research
Great. And also wanted to ask about the academic end market. I know that's been very stable for you guys. But-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah.
Jack Meehan
Analyst, Nephron Research
Just what you're seeing in the US here with the continuing resolution for the NIH, just thoughts on the durability moving forward. Thank you.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, Jack, thanks for noticing that. That was a real bright spot for us. We actually grew, I think, 2% in the quarter. You know, this is. We've been working on this thing for some time to really build out our portfolio and really change our market position in academic research, and I think it's starting to show up in the numbers. I think stabilization really is what we're seeing, which is the funding is there. You know, NIH is a relatively really small part of Agilent business, so really is immaterial.
But we're seeing, you know, universities have increasingly been funded through private sectors, so the money, money is there, and even so we saw money in China as well.
So it was really a nice global story for us, and we're fairly optimistic that that kind of stabilization can be there for us for the rest of the year.
Operator
Your next question will come from the line of Doug Schenkel with Wolfe Research. Please go ahead.
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
Well, Mike and Padraig, congrats to both of you. Mike, as everyone said, you'll be missed. I hope this means more time on the beach, but we'll miss you.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Absolutely. I'll be listening.
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
Yeah. Yeah. I hope not too much. But anyway, I want to ask a question on guidance and then a question on capital deployment. And
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Sure, absolutely. Go ahead, Doug.
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
Yeah, so for the year, on one hand, around 48% of sales is in the first half, at least that's how you've guided, I believe. Yeah, that's lower than last year, but it's not outside the norm for the last several years. On the other hand, you know, just doing some math, your guidance for the first half embeds the assumption that, you know, revenue declines around 7% organically and then improves, you know, 7 to 9% positive organic in the second half.
Can you just do that just as a function of the comps, or do you actually really need to see improvement in, you know, certain geographies or certain end markets or categories? And then again, just a math question: Does guidance assume Q4 revenue kind of exiting around, like, $1.8 billion?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Well, hey, hey, Doug, this is Bob. I'll take that last one. We'll tell you when we get to Q4. You know what I would say, but your math is, in all seriousness, spot on as usual. I think one of the things that we look at is we look at it a couple of different ways. I think the way to look at it is that, you know, first half, second half, kind of looking at seasonality, that's probably more instructive given kind of the changes in the growth rates. When you look at it, as you noticed, as you mentioned, it is in line with our historical seasonality.
And when you look at the growth rates, you are, you're right, we are expecting growth in the back half of the year. A lot of that is, in fact, the easier compares. And when we actually look at... What I would ask you to take a look at also is a two-year stack basis relative to-
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
Mm-hmm.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
You know, implied Q1 and Q, or first half and second half, and what you would see there is a much more smooth number, that we also looked at as well. So as usual, you're spot on there.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
And Bob, I think that's why, you know, we really emphasize in this script, you know, the word stabilization, because as we have continued stabilization, you know, we're gonna get a lift on the growth rate just by the comps as we go.
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
... That's super helpful. Yeah, I just know there's a lot of focus on how much improvement is necessary to get there. So if a lot of this is stability and just math, that I think obviously makes people more comfortable. I know I've taken up a lot of airtime already. Real quick, capital deployment. You know, the cash flow remains robust, the balance sheet is super clean. Can you just talk about your thinking right now on capital deployment and what the environment looks like right now?
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, I think we remain very interested in deploying capital in a balanced way, which is inclusive of investing in the business. That speaks directly to our interest in M&A. It's our build and buy growth strategy. I'd just have to say that the funnel pipeline is more robust than I've seen in a number of years. You know, nothing to obviously announce, but we're very much engaged.
Doug Schenkel
Managing Director, Wolfe Research
Great. Thanks again.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Mm-hmm.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Josh Waldman with Cleveland Research. Please go ahead.
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
Hey, thanks for taking my questions, and
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Sure.
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
Congratulations, Mike and Padraig.
Padraig McDonnell
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Thank you.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah. Thank you.
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
Yeah. Yeah, just a couple on my end, and maybe Bob, starting with you. First, a follow up on the guide. Can you comment a bit more on how Q2 guide moved versus the framework in the initial outlook? I assume core outlook came down a bit, but just wanted to confirm the moving pieces there. And then does the guide, the core guide, reflect any changes in Q3 or Q4, or is it really just reflecting an update on H1?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, that's a good question. It's a little of both. Josh, so Q1 - Q2 is relatively intact for what we had originally thought, with the exception of that, you know, small movement of the China business. That's roughly a point of core growth from, you know, Q1 and Q2 switching. What I would say is, you know, Q1 also had a beat into it, and what we're taking is some of that out of the second half of the year.
So the takeaway is Q2 is spot on from where we expected it to be, absent that kind of shifting, the timing shift of China, and then the Q2 or the rest of Q1 kind of the beat really helps us in the second half of the year.
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
Okay. Okay. And then, Mike, can you talk about how visibility in the business has evolved over the last three months? Has there been any improvements in the ability of the funnel to predict near-term sales, or still seeing an elongation of, you know, kind of opportunity and quoting flipping to orders? Year to year-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
... total company, and then also what you're seeing in pharma, specifically.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, no, and I'll have Padraig jump in as well. I think the biz still remains the same. I don't think it's any better, any worse. And so I think it's the normal kind of cadence of business. And that's why, as Bob just mentioned, you know, when we're talking about the second half, you know, we bank some of the beat to, you know, to and put against the second half because we've yet to see the second half materialize in terms of the order book, which is typical at this time of year.
Padraig McDonnell
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, no, I think, I think that's right, Mike, and I think, as far as the quality of orders remains, that remain in our backlog, nothing has changed. We've not seen any increase in cancellations, and, ex-China, the funnel continues to grow, and that's led by the aftermarket business. I will say, you know, as a continuing theme, the deal closure times remain at an elevated levels-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Mm-hmm.
Padraig McDonnell
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
But it's definitely stable, and deal win rates have been consistent.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah. I think it's a very important point made here. Elevated, but we're not seeing elongation. So, you know, they're, they're stable, but they're longer than they have been in the past.
Josh Waldman
Analyst, Cleveland Research
Okay. Thanks, guys.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Sure.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Dan Leonard with UBS. Please go ahead.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
Thank you. My first question, just a bit more on China. Are you expecting sequential growth in Q2 in China, similar to Q1?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
No. If you looked at the sequential number, it's gonna be roughly the same as what we had in Q, in Q1.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
If that was good.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
Uh, thank-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yep.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
All right. Thank you for that. And Mike, congrats on your retirement. I was wondering if you could elaborate on timing. You know, I was surprised; others were surprised. I've gotten the question a number of times, and would just love to hear your thoughts.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, thanks for that. So, you know, while it's maybe a surprise to many on the call, and it was a surprise when I shared the news across the company, because, you know, the Agilent team just knows how much I love working for this company and work with them. And it really was a hard, it was a really difficult decision for me, but, you know, I've been contemplating this for a while.
And, you know, I pulled the board into the discussion, started communicating with them, 'cause I really wanted to make sure that they had enough time to really run a thorough and thoughtful selection process, which they're able to do. And, in my mind, they came out with the best possible choice in selecting Padraig.
Yeah, this is something that I've been contemplating for a while, and then started engaging the board about my timing, and then really wanna make sure they had enough time to, you know, really pick the right successor, and that's what they did.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
Well, you always seem to be having a lot of fun, so, congrats again-
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Uh.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
And it's been good.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Thank you. It's gonna be hard to step away, but I have to say, the pull of family was just too strong. We have an eighteen-month-old grandson, and he will soon have a brother and sister, so there's a lot going on the family side, and there's only one way I could make more time. So again, it's been a real pleasure working with all of you on the call.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
All right. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from the line of Luke Sergott with Barclays. Please go ahead.
Luke Sergott
Director of Healthcare Equity Research, Barclays
Great. Thanks, guys, for squeezing me in. I just want to talk about the margins on the quarter and kind of the step down in DGG and LSAG. And I assume, you know, obviously, it's probably driven by the volume declines there on the instrument side. But, you know, how you guys view the recovery in the margins between DGG and LSAG throughout the year to hit your guide?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah. Hey, Luke, this is Bob, just real quick. You're right. If I look at DGG, it actually was improvement year over year, but it was down, and it was really a result of that margin or the volume. I would say also, there was an element of mix in LSAG, and I would expect that to continue to improve. You know, the cost actions that we took weren't fully actualized all in, in, as expected in Q1, so we'll have the full impact of those as well in Q2 throughout.
So I would expect an improvement over the course of the year as volumes grow up in both LSAG and DGG.
Luke Sergott
Director of Healthcare Equity Research, Barclays
That's what I thought. I just wanted to clear up. And then just for follow-up here from the Q2 guide, can you just help frame what you guys are embedded there by the different segments?
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah, if I look at the Q2 guide, you know, we're still expecting that if I look at the end market, you know, pharma down double digits, academia and government down low single digits, really as a result of some of that timing shift. Diagnostics and clinical down mid-singles, and chemical and advanced materials down high single digits, and food about the same. Both of those are, you know, as a result of some of the shift also in the China business from, you know, Q2 back into Q1, and then environmental and forensics, you know, kind of mid-single-digit decline.
Dan Leonard
Analyst, UBS
Great. Thanks.
Bob McMahon
CFO, Agilent Technologies
Yep.
Operator
Our final question will come from the line of Paul Knight with KeyBanc. Please go ahead.
Paul Knight
Managing Director, KeyBanc
Hey, Mike, really super to see you doing what you're doing. And I knew you, I don't know, fifteen years before you became CEO. So I guess the concluding question I would have, at least professionally, would be, what do you see in terms of two things? Number one, what do you think the kind of market growth rate is for the markets that Agilent participates in? And then geographically, where do you see the surprise over the next five years? Like, will Japan reinvigorate its growth?
Will Europe see more insourcing? Would love to have your perspective on those things.
Mike McMullen
President and CEO, Agilent Technologies
Yeah. Hey, thanks, Paul. Yeah, we do go way back, don't we? And it's been great to work with you over those years, going way back to the CAG days in my prior role. You know, I think we think this is a, you know, 4% to 6% kind of growth market, you know, mid-singles. So we think that the kind of market growth that we're not experiencing as an industry right now is an anomaly, and this will be back to that, you know, 4% to 6% kind of long-term growth rate.
Obviously, certain segments within that overall macro number, that Big Ten will be growing faster than that, and that's always a challenge to make sure that you pick those segments, so you can actually beat that number.
I think there's gonna be some geographic mix. I mean, we've, we've, you know, evolved our view of, of long-term growth into China because we actually expect, you know, with some of the supply chain moves and other things, that have been going on, that you'll see, a growth, more growth in, in Europe, which has been, you know, more of a slower grower for us geographically. But we've been continuing to be surprised how well we do, our team does in Europe.
I think you're going to expect to see, Japan, rejuvenated, particularly. I think you can make the case of the semi industry, which is gonna return with some strength, in Japan.
But that's the beauty of this business, is just the diversified nature of both the end markets and geographies. So, that would be my last, I guess, my final prediction of long-term growth for the market in this role. But thanks, Paul, appreciate the comments, and looking forward to staying in touch.
Operator
I'll now turn the call back over to Parmeet Ahuja for closing remarks.
Parmeet Ahuja
Vice President of Investor Relations, Agilent Technologies
Thank you, Regina, and thanks, everyone, for being on the call today. With that, we'd like to close the call. Have a good day, everyone.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes today's call. Thank you all for joining.
